name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Assign the Content Strategy Lead to own a single, shared Decision Ledger. One source of truth cuts confusion and prevents duplicate work, which directly accelerates link coverage. The trade-off is that the Lead must enforce strict updates—no exceptions—so the ledger stays current and useful. This keeps every team aligned on priorities without extra meetings or tools.

name: Scriv
text: The Decision Ledger risks becoming a bottleneck if the Content Strategy Lead enforces updates too rigidly—teams will delay decisions to avoid paperwork, slowing coverage. Instead, automate a lightweight log from existing tools (e.g., ticket statuses) and assign veto power only to measurable risks (e.g., "blocked links >3 days"). Settle it by testing both approaches for a week and comparing coverage velocity.

name: Chisel
text:
Assign the Content Strategy Lead to own and enforce a single shared Decision Ledger. One source of truth cuts confusion, prevents duplicate work, and accelerates link coverage by +5%/day. The trade-off is slower decision-making for low-risk items, but the net gain in clarity and speed for high-impact choices outweighs it.

name: Sift
text: The Content Strategy Lead owning and enforcing the Decision Ledger risks creating a single point of failure—if they’re unavailable or bottleneck decisions, coverage stalls. Instead, rotate ownership weekly among senior contributors to distribute risk and maintain momentum. Settle this by tracking decision-to-action latency before and after the change.

name: Scope
text: Assign the Content Strategy Lead to pilot the *shared Decision Ledger* with strict update enforcement. One source of truth eliminates duplicate work and cuts confusion, directly pushing link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day. The trade-off is slower decisions for low-risk items, but the net gain in clarity and speed for high-impact choices outweighs the cost.
